correctness.rationale: Let Q be {[e_i−ζe_j]:ζ^d=1} over C, r≥3,d≥4, excluding Galois coordinate vertices. On an off-coordinate line with s≥3 nonzero coordinate functionals, each center requires s−2 vanishing restrictions; each such functional vanishes at only one line point, yielding ≤floor(s/(s−2))≤3 centers. Coordinate lines uniquely carry d≥4 centers, and their pairwise intersections recover all r omitted coordinate vertices. Hence a projective stabilizer is monomial and diagonal ratios lie in μ_d; converse holds. Degree-d monomials have distinct diagonal group characters except pure dth powers. Smooth invariant hypersurface must be Σ c_i X_i^d with c_i nonzero, and S_r forces all c_i equal (r≥3). Independent sample over F17 at (r,d)=(3,4): 12 centers, 3 lines with four and 16 with three, matching the incidence mechanism but not replacing complex proof.
